nodes.label: Runtime separation
nodes.rationale: A Minecraft server mixes three workloads with opposite requirements: gameplay needs deterministic tick ordering, networking and disk IO need concurrency, chunk generation and lighting need raw CPU parallelism. Blocking one runtime stalls ticks for every connected player. Rejected alternatives: running gameplay on async tasks (loses tick ordering guarantees) and doing chunk work inline on Tokio workers (stalls all players). Threading contract stated in AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md and enforced by review; crates/pumpkin/src/main.rs carries the warning that Rayon calls from the Tokio runtime must be non-blocking. Debugging stalls means inspecting three pools (Tokio workers, Rayon workers, tick); --features console-subscriber helps on the Tokio side.

nodes.label: Sync tick game logic
nodes.rationale: Game logic (BlockBehaviour, ItemBehaviour, Goal methods) runs synchronously inside the tick on the tick thread(s) for deterministic ordering. New AI or block code must not spawn background tasks that mutate AI or world state after its scheduled turn (CONTRIBUTING 'State ownership and queries').

nodes.label: Async IO on Tokio
nodes.rationale: Networking, disk IO, plugins and events are async on Tokio. Sync locks and DashMap guards are never held across .await so Tokio workers are never blocked; a blocked worker stalls ticks for every player.

nodes.label: Rayon CPU work
nodes.rationale: CPU-heavy work (chunk generation, lighting) runs on Rayon; results cross to Tokio through channels. The canonical crossing pattern is Level::fetch_chunks. Never call blocking Rayon entry points (e.g. par_iter) from a Tokio worker.

nodes.label: Level::fetch_chunks
nodes.rationale: Canonical pattern for crossing Rayon CPU results back to the Tokio runtime through channels.

nodes.label: Client-authoritative movement
nodes.rationale: The server applies the client-reported position/rotation instead of simulating the owning player's movement. Rejected: full server-authoritative movement like vanilla (costs server CPU on the hottest path since every player moves every tick, adds player latency; performance is a stated project goal) and per-case hybrid validation (each deviation needs its own port and maintenance burden; no evidence in repo). Anti-cheat hardening would require a new superseding ADR. This deviation is part of the definition of correct in this codebase: vanilla parity holds except where a documented deviation overrides it. Server-side checks still govern what the client does not own (collisions of other entities, server teleports, knockback, external forces). Sending the server's copy of a player's state back to that same player fights client-side prediction; movement-affecting ports must only touch server-owned parts; real-client checks are required since bots and unit tests cannot verify movement feel.

nodes.label: Generated game data pipeline
nodes.rationale: Block and item properties, entity dimensions, tags, recipes, loot tables and sounds change every Minecraft update; copies pasted into server code silently go stale. Rejected: hardcoding values in source (silently stale on every update) and reading values from a vanilla jar at runtime (per-start dependency on Mojang distribution servers; build-time datapack extraction already covers it). Exception: values vanilla itself hardcodes as static final Java constants that stay stable across versions remain named Rust constants keeping the Java name; engine-definable values (world height, dimension limits) are never guessed. Version bumps flow Extractor to assets to codegen, not scattered code edits; CURRENT_MC_VERSION and LOWEST_SUPPORTED_MC_VERSION live in the generated packet mappings. Contributors may need to touch two repositories for a new data field; diff review focuses on the codegen tool, not the output.

nodes.label: Extractor
nodes.rationale: External Pumpkin-MC repository: a Fabric mod that dumps data from the running game to produce the JSON in assets/. New data fields absent from assets/ belong here, under the same contribution rules.

nodes.label: pumpkin-codegen
nodes.rationale: Tool at tools/pumpkin-codegen that turns assets/ JSON into crates/pumpkin-data/src/generated/. Run with cargo run --locked -p pumpkin-codegen; extend it when a value exists in assets/ but is not generated yet. Also generates WIT data and packet mappings for plugin changes.

nodes.label: pumpkin-data generated tables
nodes.rationale: crates/pumpkin-data/src/generated/ is codegen output and is never hand-edited (INV-0001); it encodes version-pinned vanilla data consumed by the whole server.

nodes.label: Entity islands
nodes.rationale: Independent groups (islands) of entities tick in parallel; entities within a group tick in list order. Needed because entity AI reads and writes shared world state: ticking interacting entities on different threads breaks ordering, merging everything forfeits parallelism. Rejected: single-threaded ticking (forfeits the multi-threading goal), lock-per-entity or global lock (contention serializes anyway; deadlocks hard to rule out with dynamic AI graphs), optimistic concurrency with retries (AI interactions are not idempotent: randomness, cooldowns, sounds). Reach bounds are a correctness contract: an incomplete report can change interaction order, so audits are re-checked whenever behaviour changes. Reach reporting must not itself consume randomness, select targets, advance timers, invoke gameplay callbacks or mutate the world.

nodes.label: entity_islands.rs
nodes.rationale: Implementation of entity island parallel ticking, located at crates/pumpkin-core/src/world/entity_islands.rs.

nodes.label: GoalReach
nodes.rationale: Declared per-tick access bounds returned by Goal::tick_reach(): distances within which the goal may search/read/affect entities and players, highest navigation speed modifier it may set, whether it may change blocks, and entity/player IDs reachable regardless of distance (links). An empty GoalReach means no additional access, never unknown access.

nodes.label: Goal::tick_reach
nodes.rationale: Goals implement Goal::tick_reach() returning a GoalReach; an unaudited goal returns None. Must be implemented up front before ticking, and must not consume randomness or mutate the world.

nodes.label: Mob::has_audited_tick
nodes.rationale: Species-level access audit flag paired with MobEntity::audited_reach; set true only after auditing the species' tick, custom AI and Brain behaviour against the declared bounds. Mobs without audited bounds use a conservative fallback with finite margins.

nodes.label: MobEntity::audited_reach
nodes.rationale: Per-entity summary of audited species-level reach, set true only after auditing against GoalReach bounds.

nodes.label: Wasm plugin platform
nodes.rationale: Pumpkin cannot load Bukkit or Fabric plugins (it is not a fork of the Java server), so the plugin surface is defined from scratch, usable by external SDKs in other languages. Rejected: Bukkit/Fabric-compatible loading (those ecosystems are Java-server-bound), native dynamic libraries as the public contract (Wasm gives sandboxing, cross-language bindings and a versioned interface file that native ABIs lack), single unversioned plugin API (host crates split by API version so old plugins keep working). Event contracts are sacred: when porting gameplay a plugin could observe or cancel, existing events keep firing at the same points with the same payloads; cancellable events skip their effect when cancelled. Plugin-platform changes are cross-cutting (WIT + host + SDK + runtime + codegen) and get extra CI; v0.2 stays behind the plugin-v0_2 feature flag until its ABI is finished; plugin author documentation lives in pumpkin-plugin-api, not the server docs.

nodes.label: Public WIT contract
nodes.rationale: The WIT is the public contract: it is mirrored to its own repository and SDK bindings for other languages are generated from it, so a breaking change there breaks SDKs outside this repo. Prefer additive changes and call out anything breaking; check_wit CI validates both WIT packages with wit-bindgen/wasm-tools.

nodes.label: pumpkin-plugin-wit
nodes.rationale: Crates holding the WIT packages (API versions v0.1 and v0.2), permissively licensed, mirrored by CI to Pumpkin-MC/pumpkin-plugin-wit on every push to master (sync-wit.yml).

nodes.label: pumpkin-plugin-api
nodes.rationale: Permissively licensed SDK crate (MIT OR Apache-2.0, unlike the GPL-3.0 server) that plugin authors target; must change together with WIT and host layers.

nodes.label: pumpkin-wasm-host
nodes.rationale: Wasmtime-based host crates (pumpkin-wasm-host-v0_1 / -v0_2); each API version is a physical crate generating its own bindings so old plugins keep working while new ABIs evolve.

nodes.label: PLUGIN_API_VERSION
nodes.rationale: Constant in pumpkin-core's plugin/mod.rs; bumped on breaking changes to the native in-process plugin API (which still exists internally alongside the Wasm platform).

nodes.label: sync-wit.yml
nodes.rationale: CI workflow that subtree-mirrors the WIT directory to Pumpkin-MC/pumpkin-plugin-wit on every push to master, keeping the public contract repository in sync.

nodes.label: Carrot module system
nodes.rationale: Carrot must reproduce the Latte Studios build server behaviour delivered on Paper/Purpur by about 34 plugins (LuckPerms groups, permission-gated Skript creative, FAWE and terraforming addons, chat channels, multiworld) and cannot load any of them, so every feature is reimplemented natively in Rust. Requirements: runtime enable/disable like Paper plugins (compile-time cargo features rejected), minimal upstream diff so rebasing stays cheap (one patch stack in pumpkin-core rejected as Purpur-style rebase pain), no dependence on unstable plugin loading (libloading native plugins rejected as primary vehicle: single version integer means the .dll must match the exact server build and plugin Context does not expose world internals a WorldEdit module needs; Wasm plugins rejected for first-party features because sandboxing blocks deep world access, though they remain the supported public platform per ADR-0005). Modules are workspace crates compiled into the binary; only upstream change is the carrot::init call in crates/pumpkin/src/main.rs plus workspace/dependency entries. Enable/disable reuses the plugin machinery via synthetic plugin Context (metadata carrot-<id>): register_command with atomic dispatcher swap and command tree re-broadcast, register_event with source-tagged handlers; disabling removes handlers by source from the shared HandlerMap and unregisters tracked commands, same semantics as plugin unload. Root infrastructure commands (/carrot module list|enable|disable and group reload) are always registered so a disabled module can always be re-enabled. Group-join handler and module join handlers are registered blocking, groups first, so modules may trust group permissions are already applied. on_enable/on_disable hooks are synchronous by design; modules spawn async work onto tokio following upstream async rules. Permission nodes of disabled modules stay in the registry (harmless); handlers and commands are fully removed. Future modules (essentials, multiverse, chat, worldedit engine, terrain) plug in via register_module in crates/carrot/src/lib.rs.

nodes.label: CarrotModule trait
nodes.rationale: Trait provided by crates/carrot-core that each feature module implements; on_enable/on_disable hooks are synchronous by design.

nodes.label: ModuleContext
nodes.rationale: Context handed to modules in crates/carrot-core; gives modules plugin-like registration (commands, events, permissions) via a synthetic plugin Context with metadata carrot-<id>.

nodes.label: Carrot manager
nodes.rationale: Module manager in crates/carrot-core; features register through register_module in crates/carrot/src/lib.rs and the manager handles runtime enable/disable via the plugin machinery.

nodes.label: builder_mode module
nodes.rationale: First module delivered with ADR-0006: parity with the reference server's criativo.sk. carrot:buildermode switches a player to creative on join/respawn and others back to survival.

nodes.label: carrot.toml
nodes.rationale: Per-module enabled map in <exec_dir>/carrot/, materialized with each module's default on boot.

nodes.label: groups.toml
nodes.rationale: LuckPerms-style groups with inheritance, players by name and -node denies, in <exec_dir>/carrot/; seeded from the reference server's default/builder layout; reloaded by the group reload command.

nodes.label: Carrot permission namespace
nodes.rationale: Permissions use the carrot: namespace (carrot:admin, carrot:buildermode, ...) so the PermissionManager's existing wildcard resolution (carrot:*, carrot:module.*) applies to groups unchanged. Group permissions are applied to a player's attachment on join by a blocking handler registered before any module handler and re-applied by group reload; blocking handlers run sequentially in registration order, giving modules the ordering contract.

nodes.label: Group reload command
nodes.rationale: Reloads groups.toml at runtime; ADR-0006 names it /carrotgroups reload but the shipped code registers it as the groups reload subcommand of the root /carrot command (see GAP-0003).

nodes.label: No CI check for codegen drift
nodes.rationale: No workflow in .github/workflows/ regenerates codegen output and compares against committed files (absence verified by grepping all workflows for codegen/pumpkin-codegen), so a hand edit or stale regeneration passes CI. INV-0001 is enforced by review only; drift between assets/ and generated tables can reach master undetected and the next regeneration produces noisy, hard-to-attribute diffs. Proposed action: CI job running cargo run --locked -p pumpkin-codegen on a clean checkout and failing on git diff --exit-code -- crates/pumpkin-data/src/generated/, then flip INV-0001 from Documented-only to Enforced.
nodes.norm_label: no ci check for codegen drift

nodes.label: Bedrock support undocumented
nodes.rationale: README marks Bedrock Edition support as W.I.P. and unlike the Java side (version pinning via generated pumpkin-data plus vanilla-parity discipline) there is no documented statement of supported Bedrock protocol versions, the gameplay subset that works over Bedrock, or the applicable parity target. Impact: no documented baseline to verify Bedrock work against, vanilla-parity claims cannot extend to Bedrock, and the default-enabled Bedrock listener (port 19132) may surprise Java-only operators. Any Bedrock behaviour claim should be treated as unverified until a target is documented in docs/architecture/flows.md.

nodes.label: Bedrock protocol implementation
nodes.rationale: Bedrock protocol implementation living in crates/pumpkin-protocol/src/bedrock/ alongside the Java one; work-in-progress with no documented parity baseline.

nodes.label: carrotgroups command name mismatch
nodes.rationale: ADR-0006 decision point 5 says group reload is /carrotgroups reload, but the implemented code registers no /carrotgroups command at all: group reload is the groups reload subcommand of the root /carrot command (carrot-core/src/command.rs), and docs/minecraft/commands.md documents the code's shape. An unauthorized implementation deviation from an accepted ADR, never recorded in Phase 1-2 or later commits; anyone following the ADR gets an unknown-command error, weakening the ADR as authoritative record. Proposed: either accept the code shape (recommended, single root prefix) with a recorded correction note, or register /carrotgroups as an alias and update the commands doc. Resolution pending user decision as of 2026-11-22.

nodes.label: Generated data is never hand-edited
nodes.rationale: Every file under crates/pumpkin-data/src/generated/ is byte-for-byte the output of cargo run --locked -p pumpkin-codegen against current assets/; changes land only by changing inputs and regenerating. Rationale: a hand edit is untraceable to its data source, silently disagrees with the next regeneration, and turns every version bump into a manual merge of unknown quality; regeneration is deterministic, hand edits are not. Enforcement currently review-only (AGENTS.md 'Game data and constants' and tools/pumpkin-codegen/AGENTS.md); cheapest enforcement point is a CI job that regenerates and fails on git diff, tracked as GAP-0001.

nodes.label: Server code never unwraps or panics
nodes.rationale: No unwrap(), expect(), panic!, todo! or printing to stdout/stderr anywhere in server code including error paths; Result/Option handled for real, diagnostics through tracing. Rationale: a server that panics on reachable input takes down every player's session (panics become crash reports and force shutdown via the panic hook in crates/pumpkin/src/main.rs); unwrap/expect are exactly how panics slip into can't-happen paths; direct stdout/stderr printing corrupts the console which doubles as a command interface and bypasses log formatting and filtering. Enforced via [workspace.lints.clippy] denying unwrap_used, expect_used, panic, todo, print_stdout, print_stderr plus lint groups, crate-level #![deny(clippy::unwrap_used)] in main.rs, and CI RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings with cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features. Sanctioned exception: local #[expect(..., reason)] with a stated why; test builds may re-allow via cfg_attr(test); tools/pumpkin-fuzzer deliberately relaxes these for itself.
nodes.norm_label: server code never unwraps or panics

nodes.label: No sync locks held across await
nodes.rationale: No std::sync mutex/RwLock guard, DashMap reference guard or other blocking lock held across an .await point; data that must survive an await is cloned or the lock is reacquired after. Rationale: holding a sync lock across an await can block the Tokio worker thread or deadlock the runtime when another task holding the lock awaits the same worker, and a blocked Tokio worker stalls ticks for every player (ADR-0001). Enforcement is review-only plus incidental clippy coverage; clippy::await_holding_lock is not explicitly enabled and re-entrancy variants (navigator/Brain helper locking while holding its guard) are not catchable by any existing lint.
nodes.norm_label: no sync locks held across await

nodes.label: CI compiles warning-free
nodes.rationale: Every CI job compiles with RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings; any compiler warning anywhere CI builds fails the build. Pre-existing warnings in untouched files are tolerated locally but new warnings are not. Rationale: warnings are deferred bugs and lint noise that hide the signal reviewers need; a warning budget would erode the intentionally strict clippy policy one exception at a time. Enforced via .github/workflows/rust.yml setting RUSTFLAGS globally and clippy running --all-targets --all-features; exceptions exist only as scoped, reasoned #[expect(...)] attributes in source, never as CI configuration.

nodes.label: Plugin crate license boundary
nodes.rationale: No code from the GPL-3.0 server crates is moved, copied or paraphrased into pumpkin-plugin-api, pumpkin-plugin-wit or pumpkin-plugin-utils (MIT OR Apache-2.0), so plugin authors can depend on them permissively. Rationale: the dual licensing is deliberate (ADR-0005); plugin authors must be able to write and distribute plugins without their work being forced into GPL by a dependency; if server code leaks in, the whole permissive surface becomes legally ambiguous or effectively GPL and external SDK projects inherit the contamination. Enforcement currently review-only via AGENTS.md 'Plugin API' and license files; cheapest enforcement point is a CI guard failing when a permissive crate adds a dependency on any GPL server crate, plus periodic review for copied code.
